# Biomarkers and Registry 2.0

Registry 2.0 has 113 typed measurement definitions across 83 analytes and 637 EN/RU/ES aliases. Definition identity is analyte plus specimen, property, scale, timing, method, and value kind.

## Actual lifecycle

`worker/src/pipeline.ts` extracts laboratory rows with `extractPipelineBiomarkersFromText` or `extractPipelineBiomarkersFromImage` and first inserts raw evidence into `document_extracted_biomarkers` with `status='needs_review'`: raw label, numeric/text value, unit/raw unit, `document_id`, `profile_id`, and source page/text. A clinical axis such as specimen can be preserved only when its lexical form is captured with that row's source text or section context; an omitted structured field may be recovered from that captured row evidence, but the system never fabricates an unstated axis. Initial extraction does not call `resolveMeasurementDefinition` and does not persist a resolver outcome. Before any prospective preview, acceptance, confirmation, correction, or Registry reprocess, `prepareMeasurementEvidence` applies the effective measurement override once and derives the canonical stated axes, sentinels, reviewed panel-policy context, section support, and provenance. `document_type` remains on `documents.document_type`, not on an extracted laboratory row.

Each page stores `ocr_text`. A transcribed heading is kept as `section_context` only when that heading occurs in the matching page OCR; a fabricated heading cannot unlock a specimen. After the stated-evidence filter, reviewed policy `cbc_whole_blood` may supply `whole_blood` only for its allowlisted analytes and records `specimen_from_reviewed_panel`; conflicts are hard resolver evidence failures. Biochemistry headings do not become serum or plasma, and the Resolver never rematches a raw heading. Registry reprocessing does not recapture headings on historical rows.

`GET /api/documents/[id]/biomarkers` returns the raw extracted row and computes a `buildNormalizationReview` preview. Preview is not persistence. Explicit acceptance (`POST .../biomarkers/accept`), correction or confirmation (`PATCH .../biomarkers`), and operator Registry batch reprocessing use the same prepared evidence for the Resolver, persisted decision trace, and writer payload. Each persists one source-linked observation and an active normalization revision for `resolved`, `partial`, `ambiguous`, or `unmapped`: raw evidence and document linkage remain on the observation; result/trace remain on the revision and project back to the extracted row. Revision input identity is a nullable, validated v1 SHA-256 over an allowlisted canonical evidence record; OCR text, raw heading text, confidence, action, and release metadata are not identity inputs.
The review UI draws a source-region overlay only for persisted, page-coherent exact positional provenance on the displayed page. Fuzzy, ambiguous, model-origin, cross-page, legacy, missing-layer, and invalid regions remain page-only so the UI never presents an unverified rectangle as fact; pointer hover and keyboard focus do not navigate or scroll, while explicit selection retains the page affordance.

## Resolver outcomes and consumers

| outcome | concrete definition | verification | default record lifecycle | Health Profile |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resolved` | concrete reviewed definition | `user_verified` on acceptance; `auto_verified` only from the approved service quality gate | `active` | eligible only when verified, numeric, source-range-backed, and covered by a reviewed compatible binding |
| `partial` | none; analyte tier only if supplied by resolver | `pending` | `active` until an explicit lifecycle transition | not eligible |
| `ambiguous` | none; analyte tier only if supplied by resolver | `pending` | `active` until an explicit lifecycle transition | not eligible |
| `unmapped` | none | `pending` | `active` until an explicit lifecycle transition | not eligible |

## Document review and lifecycle

`GET /api/documents/[id]/biomarkers` and document bootstrap responses expose `recordStatus`, `sourceIsCurrent`, persisted or preview `decisionSource`, `decisionQuality`, `decisionNotPersisted`, `decisionQualityCodes`, and `actionAvailability`. The review UI renders resolver outcome, verification status, and record lifecycle as independent labels. Raw acceptance keeps incomplete evidence without verification; rejection requires an owner-scoped reason and current source/revision confirmation; automatic verification is service-only. Once every current published extracted row leaves `needs_review` or `pending_review`, the acceptance endpoint transitions the document from `needs_review` to `ready` / `completed`; a partial acceptance leaves the document reviewable and the action available.

`rejected` and `superseded` are record-lifecycle states, not verification statuses. Their source rows remain available as historical/raw evidence with stable non-PII reason codes, but are read-only and excluded from current observation, batch-verification, correction, reversal, and Health Profile projections. Reprocessing uses the stored prior input identity and records independent input, outcome, and release facts; release-only changes are audit-only unless the operator explicitly requests `--release-refresh`. Apply rechecks the complete five-field deployed release tuple atomically before writer materialization and durably aborts on drift. Historical undo restores a selected persisted revision through its own CAS-protected RPC instead of rerunning current Resolver or panel-policy logic.

## Health Profile projection

`GET /api/health-profile` admits laboratory input only through `projectHealthProfileLaboratoryAdmission`. The source must be current and active, have an active `resolved` trace whose selected candidate matches the measurement definition, use reviewed Registry v2 provenance, have a reviewed compatible assessment binding, and be `auto_verified`, `user_verified`, or `manually_corrected`. Numeric values must be finite and retain a usable printed reference range; comparator or detection-limit results such as `< 0.20` are admitted as text markers with `value: null` and never contribute a numeric score. Admission and score contribution are separate: an admitted marker may still be non-scoreable under Registry role, readiness, specimen, or range policy. `GET /api/biomarkers` returns a stable assessment-admission decision and the canonical exclusion reason from the same projection.

Chart-facing `GET /api/biomarkers` and `GET /api/health-profile` responses emit `Cache-Control: no-store`, so corrections are not served from an HTTP cache. Health Profile reads the latest assessment, job, and synthesis state without generating synthesis during `GET`. The score/readiness policy receives admitted assessment candidates plus explicit `asOf`, `evaluatedAt`, the immutable freshness policy, and a read-only Registry 2.0 snapshot; it selects the latest candidate by assessment identity, classifies factual freshness, evaluates required-group readiness, computes score/confidence aggregates, and returns selected markers plus provenance and exclusions. Job lifecycle is a separate display axis: when a completed version exists and a queued or processing recalculation is running, `assessment.display_state` is `outdated` while the completed named-system and overall scores remain visible.
After admission, `projectHealthProfileAssessmentRead` owns persisted-versus-fallback interpretation and returns `assessment.display_state`, `has_current_version`, status, error, version, and freshness metadata as one read projection; legacy or policy-incompatible payloads use the fallback snapshot without changing Registry admission or score/readiness policy. Profile and dashboard clients consume this projected lifecycle state rather than recomputing it.
`Historical reads use one persisted-decision reader: an active revision is authoritative and exposes independent `source` (`persisted`, `preview`, `none`) and `quality` (`available`, `unavailable`, `conflict`). Preview is explicit and non-persisted; missing or conflicting historical evidence is reported without current Resolver fallback, and concrete consumers fail closed when current catalog enrichment is unavailable.`

## Unknown labels and controlled reprocessing

An unknown label remains raw extracted evidence and becomes persisted `unmapped` only after acceptance or explicit Registry batch reprocessing. `scripts/reprocess-batch.ts` invokes the operator-controlled batch path; `--release-refresh` is the explicit opt-in for creating a revision when only the release tuple changed. There is no HTTP Registry-batch endpoint, automatic catalog-change reprocessing, automatic catalog growth from patient or LLM input, admin queue promoting unknown labels, or source-document-to-catalog provenance promotion.

## Locales, units, and legacy

Aliases carry explicit EN/RU/ES locale metadata. Russian uses Unicode-aware label normalization; Spanish accent-fold fallback is collision-gated. Laboratory restrictions never replace locale metadata. Missing units follow each definition policy; conversions are reviewed presentation rules and do not erase raw evidence.

Registry v1 is frozen compatibility history. The authoritative [v1.0.0 audit](../../registry/biomarker-registry/v1.0.0/AUDIT.md) holds its 113 concepts; this guide does not duplicate them. A v1 item is never automatically promoted, admitted as an alias, or used as a runtime fallback.
